## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷasutasomajātaka* (Ja 525) is a canonical birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the traditional framework recorded in the commentary, the Buddha delivered this tale while residing at Jetavana to illustrate the practice of self-abnegation and renunciation, featuring an introductory story that corresponds to that of the *Mahānāradakassapajātaka*. In Pali exegetical works such as the *Buddhavaṁsa-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Jātakanidānakathā*, the life of Cūḷasutasoma is cited as a prime illustration of the Bodhisatta's perfection of renunciation (*nekkhamma-pāramī* or *nekkhamma-paramaṭṭha-pāramī*), grouped alongside other prominent renouncers such as Hatthipāla, Somanassa, and Ayoghara [Endo 1997; Dutt 1956; Gaffney 2003; War Yar Mein Da 2015].

The central thematic climax of the tale is epitomized in a verse quoted in the *Jātakanidāna*, wherein the Bodhisatta abandons supreme royal power without attachment: having obtained a great kingdom, he casts it away like a glob of spittle (*mahārajjaṁ hatthagataṁ kheḷapiṇḍaṁ va chaḍḍayiṁ* / *cajato na hoti laggaṁ, esā me nekkhammapāramī*) [Gaffney 2003; War Yar Mein Da 2015].

Text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus identify extensive Pali-internal alignment, sharing 60 matching passages with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Pañcamo bhāgo) as well as verse overlap with the *Candakumārajātaka* (Ja 544) [DharmaNexus]. Across language corpora, DharmaNexus detects automated matches with several Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese texts, including the Sanskrit *Suvarṇaprabhāsasūtra*, the Tibetan translation of the *Pūrṇaparipṛcchāsūtra* (D0061), Kṣemendra's *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155), the Tibetan *Udānavarga*, and passages in the Chinese *Dīrghāgama* (T 1), *Ekottarikāgama* (T 125), and *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 100) [DharmaNexus].
